subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load

question: Should legacy `auth-profiles.json` be imported during normal auth runtime loads, or must recovery stay in doctor/startup migration before runtime reads?
rationale: The reported auth breakage is credible, but the proposed fix changes a credential-bearing runtime boundary that current tests, docs, and repository policy keep inside migration/doctor repair.

options.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
options.body: Rework the fix into doctor or an explicit startup/update migration boundary that verifies SQLite persistence and handles legacy JSON cleanup or warnings.

options.title: Approve Runtime Import
options.body: Accept runtime fallback only with maintainer/security approval plus updated invariant tests, docs, and a clear stale-credential threat model.

options.title: Pause For Canonical Issue
options.body: Pause this branch while the broader remaining migration and fallback diagnostics are handled through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100067.

recommendation.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
recommendation.body: Rework the fix into doctor or an explicit startup/update migration boundary that verifies SQLite persistence and handles legacy JSON cleanup or warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the SQLite auth-store surface and have the strongest history signal on the runtime persistence boundary.
